annotations.text:
Both variants sit on the same two pieces:

• UserIdentity (libs/ui) — avatar + two lines
• the UserSelect popup — server search, 20 rows, honest "showing N of 46" footer

Only the container differs: a chips field vs a list of rows.

Where each one earns its place

Inline — dense forms, few guests, no per-person state to show. Keeps the 36px row rhythm.

Stacked — the event sheet, where each guest carries an RSVP badge and the organiser is an exception the row shape can hold.

They are not rivals: one component, two layouts.

Still open

1. Does guest order mean anything? Drag needs a stored position, otherwise it is a promise the API does not keep.

2. Reorder from the keyboard (Alt + arrows) — drag alone locks out anyone not using a mouse.

3. Avatars in the calendar contract: attendees currently carry no avatarUrl, so every face is initials.
